results.title: 3D hybrid imaging system could address limitations of MRI , CT and...
results.content: In a proof-of-concept study, researchers from the Keck School of Medicine of USC and the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) have shown that an innovative, noninvasive technique can be used to quickly collect 3D images of the human body, from head to foot. Our team has identified key limitations of existing techniques and developed a novel approach to address them," said Charles Liu, MD, Ph.D., professor of clinical neurological surgery, urology and surgery at the Keck School of Medicine, director of the USC Neurorestoration Center and co-senior author of the new research. For the first time in humans, the research team combined two imaging methods, rotational ultrasound tomography (RUST) and photoacoustic tomography (PAT), to create what they call RUS-PAT. A 3D hybrid imaging system combining rotational ultrasound tomography and photoacoustic tomography enables rapid, noninvasive imaging of both tissue and blood vessels across various body regions. This approach offers advantages over MRI, CT, and conventional ultrasound, including lower cost, absence of ionizing radiation, and improved image detail, though further refinement is needed for clinical use.
